![](asset:P000116-stem-1)A vertical projectile experiences a retarding acceleration of $a$ opposite to the direction of motion of the projectile. If the speed of projection is $u$, then:
(i) Time of ascent
(ii) Time of descent
(iii) Maximum height reached
(iv) Speed just before it hits the ground
(v) Point D and E are at same height during upward and downward motion of projectile. Which point will have greater speed?

answer.text: $t_{a} = \frac{u}{g + a}$; $t_{d} = \frac{u}{\sqrt{g^{2} - a^{2}}}$; Max height H: $\frac{u^{2}}{2(g + a)}$; Speed at C: $\sqrt{2(g - a)H} = u\sqrt{\frac{g - a}{g + a}}$; (v) Point D: the speed at D (going up) is greater than at E (coming down), because the retarding acceleration removes speed throughout the flight

assets.alt: A ball thrown up with speed u from A rises to its top point B and comes down to C, next to A. Points D (going up) and E (coming down) are at the same height. Gravity g points down.
A projectile goes up from A to the top B and comes down to C. Going up its retardation is g + a; coming down its acceleration is g − a. D and E are at the same height on the way up and down.
Velocity–time graph: a steep line from u down to zero at t_a, then a gentler line down to −v_C at t_a + t_d. The two triangles have equal areas H.
